title: fix: allow session thinking and fast-mode changes with write access
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with ordinary session write access could change a conversation’s model but could not change its thinking level or fast mode. The same mismatch affected the Control UI pickers and its /think and /fast commands.

Related: #120875, which enabled write-scoped model changes while leaving effort controls admin-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

Treat `thinkingLevel` and `fastMode` as session-only write-scoped preferences in the existing shared policy, including clearing them with `null`. Gateway single/batch patches and the Control UI use that same policy. Give the context-window control its own permission check so enabling effort controls does not accidentally enable an unrelated admin-only setting.

Read-only clients remain read-only. Context-window, verbose, tool, full-permission, and unknown-field restrictions are unchanged. No configuration migration, new setting, or active-inference hot-switching is introduced.

## User Impact

Users with `operator.write` can change thinking level and fast mode without starting a new conversation or receiving administrator access. Changes are persisted session preferences for subsequent turns; the composer still disables model/effort controls while a reply is running. Existing model/provider capability validation remains in place.

Reported by @VACInc.

## Evidence

- Before the production change, the shared-policy regression had nine expected failures. Through an authenticated Gateway WebSocket, the same session accepted a model change and then rejected its thinking change with `FORBIDDEN / MISSING_SCOPE / operator.admin`.
- After the change, **244 core/Gateway tests and 110 focused UI tests passed**, covering shared scope policy, Gateway authorization, real WebSocket persistence, Control UI access, composer interactions, and slash commands. Coverage includes on/off/auto, reset-to-default, persisted session identity, read-only denial, and mixed privileged-patch rejection.
- The composer regression renders read/write/admin clients and exercises thinking, fast-mode, and context-window callbacks against the selected session. The new cases now live in focused permission/effort test files; all 41 split-suite tests passed, followed by a passing final organization-scope rerun.
- An additional 435 existing new-session and chat-rendering tests passed, covering the other shared-picker consumer. After correcting typed fixture metadata and the chat-send fixture, 381 composer/chat-send tests passed (including rerun composer coverage).
- Independent autoreview: no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings.
- All selected quality checks passed: core/core-test/UI types, changed-file lint, UI style/i18n checks, unused exports, import cycles, schema/storage guards, runtime helpers, and auth/webhook guards. Passing checks were reused; after the test-file size failure, focused type/lint reruns and the remaining planned checks passed. No lint suppressions or baselines were changed. `git diff --check` passed.

Commands:
```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/session-method-scopes.test.ts src/gateway/method-scopes.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/lib/session-method-access.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-command-executor.test.ts src/shared/session-method-scopes.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/new-session/model-control.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.effort-scopes.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.permissions.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane-session-controls.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts -t "write-scoped operators manage"
```

Production delta: **+13 lines**, principally the independent context-window permission wiring; tests counted separately. No styling or layout changes. This is isolated Gateway and rendered UI test proof, not a deployed-Gateway or paid-provider live test.
